run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: Within the authorized window (2026-11-21T13:00:23Z to 2026-11-22T13:00:23Z) the two named indices and the connected cluster contain no record of the alerting subject (app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha, cluster us-prod-eks), and no deployment in the connected cluster occurred during the incident window. The inventory index returned exactly three in-window records, all cluster 'ci-cd' / namespace 'ci' (gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server, all status Running), and the change history returned exactly three changes in the same namespace: a jenkins LTS bump at 07:00:11Z, an argocd-server security patch at 08:00:11Z and a gitlab-runner scale 2->3 replicas at 11:00:11Z, the latest of which still precedes the alert by about one and a half hours. Nothing in the available evidence ties any of those changes to an online-device decline, and none of them is the app named in the alert. In the connected cluster every one of 24 deployments reports ready and available replicas equal to desired, all 32 pods are Running and Ready and the otel-demo pods and ReplicaSets date from 2026-11-20, i.e. no rollout in the window; the flagd fault-injection flags are all present but default to 'off', which is counter-evidence for an injected fault in this cluster. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query, so error-rate, latency and trace evidence could not be checked. No root cause is established; the deployment the alert blames is not visible in any data source available to this Run.

claims.text: The inventory index app-235-cluster-inventory holds 6 documents, and inside the authorized window it returned exactly 3, all with cluster 'ci-cd' and namespace 'ci': gitlab-runner (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, 3 replicas, status Running, last_updated 2026-11-22T11:00:11Z), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, 1 replica, Running, 2026-11-22T07:00:11Z) and argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, 2 replicas, Running, 2026-11-22T07:00:11Z). No record in that window names app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha or cluster us-prod-eks.

The change-history index app-235-change-history holds 4 documents, and inside the authorized window it returned exactly 3 changes, all changed_by 'infra-team', namespace 'ci', cluster 'ci-cd': BUILD-7X4Q9M jenkins 2.426.2-lts -> 2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-22T07:00:11Z ('Jenkins LTS version bump to 2.426.3'), BUILD-3NR8Y1 argocd-server v2.9.2 -> v2.9.3 at 2026-11-22T08:00:11Z ('ArgoCD security patch update'), and BUILD-5PW2K6 gitlab-runner scale 2 -> 3 at 2026-11-22T11:00:11Z ('Scaled gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas for faster pipeline throughput'). The most recent of these is timestamped 2026-11-22T11:00:11Z.

In the connected cluster, all 24 deployments report ready and available replicas equal to their desired replica count, including the otel-demo services (frontend, checkout, payment, cart, ad, currency, email, quote, shipping, product-catalog, recommendation, image-provider, frontend-proxy, load-generator) and the monitoring components prometheus, jaeger, otel-collector, kube-state-metrics and flagd.

All 32 pods in the connected cluster are phase Running with container ready=true and lastState reason null; the otel-demo pods started 2026-11-20T16:32 (e.g. frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, flagd-d6485586b-9t42n), and the only pods started on 2026-11-22 are the kube-system control-plane pods at 08:04:14Z. No otel-demo pod restarted or was recreated during the incident window.

Every ReplicaSet in namespace otel-demo was created on 2026-11-20 (16:32-16:33Z) and the two legacy sets with desired 0 (otel-collector-845f9747bd, prometheus-547d4cbb8) are older still, so no deployment rolled out new pods in the 2026-11-21T13:00:23Z-2026-11-22T13:00:23Z window.
The only node, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports the Ready condition True.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) defines fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with state ENABLED, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off' (paymentFailure's 'off' variant value is 0, the others false or 0).

The connected cluster's Prometheus configuration has no loaded alerting content: the prometheus ConfigMap's data.rules is '{}' and data.alerts is '{}', and its data.alerting_rules.yml returned null, while prometheus.yml lists /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml among rule_files; alertmanager.yml merely routes all alerts to the opspilot webhook. So the reported alert onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease is not produced by this cluster's rule set.

No workload matching lambda, dashboard, clientorg or grafana exists in the connected cluster: filtering all deployments on those names returned an empty list, and the cluster's namespaces are only default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo. The alerting subject therefore cannot be inspected in this cluster.

Considered and set aside: the gitlab-runner scale change BUILD-5PW2K6 (2 -> 3 replicas at 2026-11-22T11:00:11Z, cluster ci-cd, namespace ci) as the trigger. It targets a CI runner in a different cluster from the alert's us-prod-eks, its timing is about one and a half hours before the alert's reported start, and no error or failure evidence for gitlab-runner was observed or obtainable; nothing ties it to an online-device count for clientorg-alpha.

Considered and set aside: the argocd-server v2.9.2 -> v2.9.3 security patch BUILD-3NR8Y1 (2026-11-22T08:00:11Z) and the jenkins 2.426.2-lts -> 2.426.3-lts bump BUILD-7X4Q9M (2026-11-22T07:00:11Z) as the trigger. Both are ci-cd cluster / ci namespace tooling changes that precede the alert's start by five or more hours, the inventory shows both workloads Running with their expected replica counts, and no error signal tying either to the alerting workload was observed.

The most plausible remaining candidate is a change in the alerting cluster itself (us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha) that no available source covers: neither app-235-cluster-inventory nor app-235-change-history contains any us-prod-eks record inside the authorized window, and the connected Kubernetes target hosts only the otel-demo and system namespaces. This cannot be confirmed or refuted with the delivered evidence.

Obtain inventory and change history for the cluster label us-prod-eks (or the missing 'change_history' integration) covering 2026-11-22T11:30Z-12:30Z, and check whether any deployment of lambda-dashboard-monitoring landed there just before the alert, before treating the 'started right after a deployment' statement as confirmed.

Restore the Prometheus read path (execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_series and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and Jaeger (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) so that error-rate, latency and trace evidence can be checked rather than left unknown.

gaps: The alert names cluster us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring and workload clientorg-alpha, but neither app-235-cluster-inventory nor app-235-change-history returned any record for them; both indices only describe the 'ci-cd' cluster inside the window, so the deploying object named in the alert could not be read.

The indices hold 6 (inventory) and 4 (change-history) documents in total while only 3 each were returned inside the authorized window; the older documents are outside the queryable window (the time filter on last_updated / timestamp cannot be turned off) and remain unknown.

Prometheus was unreachable for every query (get_metric_names, get_series, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error rate, request rate, latency, kube-state-metrics or label evidence could be read; absence of error series is unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans, error statuses or call edges could be inspected.

The Kubernetes events query across all namespaces returned nothing in the window (status no_data), so event-based evidence such as Evicted, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling or rollout events is unknown rather than absent.

Application logs gave no usable signal: flagd-d6485586b-9t42n, load-generator-5ff476786d-xg5nz and frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw returned zero lines (bytes_read 0) for 2026-11-22T11:00Z-13:00:23Z, and otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c had 37 lines that all fell after the window end, so runtime error text for the window is not available.

The 'change_history' integration is listed as not_integrated for this Run; only the app-235-* Elasticsearch indices were available for change data, and no Grafana/Lambda telemetry for onlineDevicesCount or clientorg-alpha is present in any queryable source.

The alert's startsAt is given only relatively ('30 minutes ago'); no alerting-rule or alert-object evidence exists in the connected cluster (prometheus data.rules and data.alerts are empty), so the exact deviation start of the onlineDevicesCount metric is unknown.

global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

content:
global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: prometheus
  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: default;kubernetes;https
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics/cadvisor
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- honor_labels: true
  job_name: kubernetes-service-endpoints
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape
  - action: drop
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape_slow
  - action: replace
    regex: (https?)
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scheme
    target_label: __scheme__
  - action: replace
    regex: (.+)
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_path
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  - action: replace
    regex: (.+?)(?::\d+)?;(\d+)
    replacement: $1:$2
    source_labels:
    - __address__
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_port
    target_label: __address__
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_param_(.+)
    replacement: __param_$1
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_label_(.+)
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    target_label: namespace
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    target_label: service
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name
    target_label: node
- honor_labels: true
  job_name: kubernetes-service-endpoints-slow
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape_slow
  - action: replace
    regex: (https?)
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scheme
    target_label: __scheme__
  - action: replace
    regex: (.+)
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_path
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  - action: replace
    regex: (.+?)(?::\d+)?;(\d+)
    replacement: $1:$2
    source_labels:
    - __address__
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_port
    target_label: __address__
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_param_(.+)
    replacement: __param_$1
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_label_(.+)
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    target_label: namespace
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    target_label: service
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name
    target_label: node
  scrape_interval: 5m
  scrape_timeout: 30s
- honor_labels: true
  job_name: prometheus-pushgateway
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: service
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: pushgateway
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_probe
- honor_labels: true
  job_name: kubernetes-services
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: service
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module:
    - http_2xx
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_probe
  - source_labels:
    - __address__
    target_label: __param_target
  - replacement: blackbox
    target_label: __address__
  - source_labels:
    - __param_target
    target_label: instance
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_label_(.+)
  - source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    target_label: namespace
  - source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    target_label: service
- honor_labels: true
  job_name: kubernetes-pods
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: pod
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape
  - action: drop
    regex: true
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape_slow
  - action: replace
    regex: (https?)
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scheme
    target_label: __scheme__
  - action: replace
    regex: (.+)
    source_labels:
